name: Tangle Teezer

lead: Tangle Teezer is a British brand of detangling hairbrush created by hairdresser Shaun Pulfrey. Its signature design is a compact, handleless brush with two tiers of flexible teeth: longer ones to work through knots and shorter ones to smooth the hair.

For looks, it gives a tidier, smoother head of hair after washing, and it is used on both straight and curly hair. The brand says the design reduces pulling and snapping compared with conventional brushes. That claim comes from the company and press coverage; no clinical trials are cited.

paras: People use it on wet hair after washing or on dry hair as part of styling, working through knots gradually. It sits alongside conditioners and leave-in products in routines for long, curly or fine hair. The brand also sells versions for fragile hair and different textures.

The brush is a styling tool with no health risks beyond the general possibility of hair breakage from aggressive brushing of any kind. Counterfeits have been an issue for the brand, according to its history.

angle.text: The brush is used to detangle hair after washing or during styling so it looks smooth and tidy. Its flexible teeth are intended to work through knots on wet or dry hair of different textures.

lead: Tangle Teezer is a hair care brand best known for its detangling brushes, the first of which, 'The Original', launched in 2007[1][2]. It was created by Shaun Pulfrey, a hair colourist who trained in Manchester and London salons, after he saw clients struggle with painful detangling[1].

The design is handleless and uses two tiers of flexible teeth, long teeth that separate knots and short teeth that smooth the hair. The brand presents it as a way to detangle wet or dry hair with less pulling and less breakage than traditional bristle brushes[1]. For appearance, that means smoother, more manageable hair and a neater finish, especially for long, curly or fine hair.

Wikipedia reports that Pulfrey began developing the brush in 2003, remortgaged his London flat for £25,000 to fund the launch, and pitched it on the BBC programme Dragons' Den in 2007 without winning investment. After the episode, the company's website crashed under demand, and about 1,500 orders followed. Boots began stocking it in 2008[2].
infobox: BIC acquired the brand in December 2024 (per Grokipedia)

paras: Grokipedia describes a patented two-tiered tooth system: long, flexible teeth for detangling and shorter, firm teeth for smoothing, in a handleless body[1]. The brand has added versions such as the Extra Gentle Detangler for fragile hair and a Plant Brush made of plant-based materials[1].

Pulfrey began his career as a colourist in 1978 and, according to Grokipedia, spent 2003 to 2006 prototyping the brush and testing it on salon clients and family[1]. Tangle Teezer Limited was formed in London in 2005, and 'The Original' debuted publicly at Salon International in late 2007[1].

After the Dragons' Den pitch, sales grew from £500,000 in 2009 to £28.6 million by March 2016, with distribution in about 70 international markets, according to Wikipedia. It won Queen's Awards for Innovation in 2012 and International Trade in 2014[2]. Wikipedia says Mayfair Equity Partners bought a majority stake for about £70 million in July 2021[2], and Grokipedia reports that BIC acquired the brand in December 2024[1].
The brand markets the brush for all hair types, including straight, wavy, curly and coily, and for use on wet or dry hair[1].
